query: What legal and copyright constraints govern scraping, storing, and sharing publicly accessible computing syllabi from Indian universities, and how should we document license/terms and acceptable reuse?

response.query: What legal and copyright constraints govern scraping, storing, and sharing publicly accessible computing syllabi from Indian universities, and how should we document license/terms and acceptable reuse?
response.answer: Scraping publicly accessible syllabi from Indian universities is generally permissible, but copyright terms must be documented. Reuse must comply with the original license, often requiring attribution. Always check specific university policies.

results.title: State law requires IU faculty to post syllabi online. Here’s what to know   - Indiana Daily Student
results.content: # State law requires IU faculty to post syllabi online. Because of a new state law, Indiana University faculty must publish their course syllabi online. During the final hours of this year’s legislative session, Indiana lawmakers added the requirement as part of the state’s two-year budget bill, without debate. According to a fall “Start of the Semester Guide”, IU adopted CourseLeaf, a curriculum and course management platform. The platform will automatically transfer course materials uploaded to the syllabus page on Canvas, a learning management system used by IU, to the public site. “Indiana University works with its campuses across the state to ensure compliance with all state and federal laws,” an IU spokesperson said. “I have no problem with being transparent, no problem with what I cover in class, but if this is going to be used for people to micromanage what we teach in class, faculty are going to be concerned,” he said. “It isn't inherently bad — faculty don’t have anything to hide in their syllabi and people will comply with the law,” Lanosga said.
